summary.plain: Belle II saw the first evidence for a very rare B decay into a kaon and two neutrinos. Because the neutrinos leave no trace, the decay is found by showing that nothing else in the event accounts for the missing energy. The measured rate is somewhat higher than the Standard Model predicts.
summary.technical: Inclusive-tag and hadronic-tag searches in 362 fb⁻¹ at the Υ(4S) combine to B(B⁺ → K⁺ νν̅) = [2.3 ± 0.5(stat) ⁺⁰·⁵₋₀.₄(syst)] × 10⁻⁵, the first evidence for the decay at 3.5σ and 2.7σ above the Standard Model expectation.

title: Evidence for B⁺ → K⁺ ν ν̅ decays
why_it_matters: A flavour-changing neutral current with a clean theoretical prediction; the mild excess over the Standard Model has become one of the most watched flavour anomalies.
